name: Madison
tagline: Isthmus Living, Progressive Culture, and Four Beautiful Seasons
description: Madison is a rare American city built on an isthmus between two pristine lakes, home to a world-class university, and consistently ranked among the best places to live in the country. The city combines Midwestern friendliness with progressive cultural energy, exceptional healthcare through UW Health, and a food scene that punches far above its weight class. While Wisconsin does have a state income tax, Madison compensates with outstanding quality of life, safety, and access to nature that few cities can match. Four distinct seasons keep life dynamic, from summer sailing to winter cross-country skiing.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – consistently ranked among America's safest cities
quickFacts.climate: Continental with warm summers, cold winters, and vivid fall foliage

housing.description: Budget studio or older 1BR in an affordable neighborhood (Elvehjem, east side, or Fitchburg)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with the occasional meal out

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan (Wisconsin uses the federal healthcare.gov marketplace), assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; above that, the full price climbs past $850 a month. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: Bike-first living with a Metro Transit fare-capped pass ($65 cap) and occasional car-share

entertainment.description: Lakes, parks, the farmers' market, and low-key local outings

1M.lifestyle: A genuinely frugal Madison life built around a small studio in a budget neighborhood and a bike rather than a car — the fare-capped Metro pass and occasional car-share cover the rest, with winter the main reason a car ever appears. Cooking at home is the norm, entertainment leans on the lakes, parks, and the farmers' market, and the healthcare line assumes marketplace income is managed to stay under the ACA subsidy cliff. Housing plus the subsidized health premium alone absorb roughly two-thirds of the budget — the classic US squeeze.

housing.description: Solid mid-market 1BR in a convenient neighborhood

dining.description: Dining out regularly across Madison's strong local scene

healthcare.description: A Silver marketplace plan, likely paid at or near full price at this income

transportation.description: A reliable used car: insurance, gas, and upkeep

entertainment.description: Concerts, the Overture Center, breweries, and weekend trips

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable step up into a solid mid-market one-bedroom, a reliable car for winter, and dining out regularly across Madison's well-regarded restaurant scene. Entertainment widens to concerts, the Overture Center, breweries, and weekend trips into the surrounding lake country. At this income the Silver plan is most likely paid at or near full, unsubsidized price. Easygoing Midwestern living without the frugality math of the lean tier.

housing.description: Quality 1BR in a walkable isthmus or near-campus location

dining.description: Frequent quality dining across the city's best casual and mid-range tables

healthcare.description: A Gold plan minimizing out-of-pocket; above the ACA cliff this trends toward unsubsidized full price — the line is intentionally padded, as US healthcare is the swing variable

transportation.description: A comfortable car for regional driving and winter reliability

entertainment.description: Travel, hobbies, events, and lake-country recreation

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, financially-independent life in one of Madison's most walkable isthmus or near-campus locations, dining out several times a week and keeping a comfortable car for regional trips and winter. A real travel-and-hobbies budget sits alongside easy access to the lakes and cultural calendar. Healthcare is the swing variable — above the ACA cliff the line trends toward unsubsidized full price, so it is intentionally padded. Genuinely comfortable, low-stress living in a mid-size college town.

housing.description: Luxury downtown high-rise 1BR with lake or Capitol views

dining.description: Near-daily dining at Madison's finest tables

healthcare.description: A premium unsubsidized plan plus concierge/direct primary care

5M.lifestyle: A luxury downtown high-rise one-bedroom with lake or Capitol views, near-daily dining at Madison's best tables, and a luxury car for getting around. Concierge or direct-primary-care medicine sits on top of a premium unsubsidized plan, weekly housekeeping handles the home, and there is a standing budget for premium leisure and travel. Upscale living in an affordable metro, where the healthcare premium buys top-tier access.

housing.description: Downtown penthouse loft, or a lakefront home in Maple Bluff or Shorewood Hills

dining.description: Private-chef dining and the region's finest restaurants

healthcare.description: Concierge medicine plus a top-tier unsubsidized domestic plan

entertainment.description: A full social and cultural calendar with travel

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke travel, club memberships, and luxury experiences

10M.lifestyle: The top of what money buys in a mid-cost Midwest college town — a downtown penthouse loft or a lakefront home in Maple Bluff or Shorewood Hills, private-chef dining, luxury vehicles with charters on demand, and full household help. Concierge medicine sits on a top-tier plan, and there is a bespoke travel-and-memberships budget on top of a full social calendar. Even here the health line is fully unsubsidized. At roughly $192k/year it is genuinely lavish.
